# Intake Brief — Need juice when the player is destroyed (AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY)

> **Status of this brief:** the operator was asked four clarifying questions
> (see Appendix) and replied "continue" without answering. Per the workflow's
> "do not block indefinitely" rule, this brief proceeds on **documented
> assumptions** (marked `[ASSUMPTION]` throughout). Open questions are retained
> in the Appendix for producer validation; the item is flagged
> `needsProducerReview` until they are resolved.

## Problem statement

When the player is destroyed the game currently plays a single particle burst
(`spawnExplosionParticles(...SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE...)`), the shared enemy
`playDestructionSound()`, and a 150% scale pulse, then immediately respawns or
ends the run. There is no camera shake, no player-specific death sound, and no
layered secondary feedback, so the most consequential event in the game feels
flat. The operator wants "lots of juice … screen shake, particle explosion, SFX
etc. Go wild!"

## Users

- **Player** — feels a weighty, unmistakable consequence when their ship is
  destroyed, distinct from ordinary enemy kills, reinforcing that a life was
  lost (or the run ended).
- **Developer / designer tuning feel** — can adjust shake intensity, sound
  layering, flash strength, and extra layers through exposed constants in one
  place without editing each death path.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, when my ship is destroyed I feel a strong impact: the
  camera shakes hard, a bright flash frames the screen, the explosion is
  visibly larger than an enemy's, and a distinct low "hull breach" boom plays
  instead of the generic enemy pop — so a life lost reads differently from a
  kill.
- As a **player**, the effect scales: losing my final life (game over) feels
  even heavier than a mid-run respawn, without becoming disorienting.
- As a **developer**, I can tune `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
  `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`, and the dedicated sound's amplitude in one
  constants module, and the behaviour is covered by unit tests so tuning does
  not silently regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Shared player-death juice helper exists:** A reusable helper
  (e.g. `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` or an extension of
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) can be invoked from a scene with
  `(scene, x, y)` and composes the full effect (screen shake + particle burst +
  flash + any additional layers), returning/recording handles so scene teardown
  can destroy them. Both player-death paths use it:
  `PlayScene._loseLife()` (real run, lives/game-over) and
  `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` (combat gym, in-place respawn).
- [ ] **AC2 — Screen shake:** A scene-camera shake is triggered on player
  destruction with a configurable intensity and duration (suggested defaults:
  intensity ~0.008–0.02, duration ~250–400 ms, full 2D). Shake strength is a
  tunable constant in one module. Verified by unit test with a camera spy
  (`camera.shake` called with the configured intensity/duration).
- [ ] **AC3 — Dedicated player-death SFX:** A new `playPlayerDestructionSound()`
  in `src/audio/effects.ts`, distinct from the generic
  `playDestructionSound()` (suggested: heavier/lower multi-layer cue — impact
  thump + descending body + brief noise tail), exposed amplitude/length as
  constants. The player-death paths call it **exactly once**; existing
  `playDestructionSound()` calls on those paths are replaced (no double-play).
  Verified by unit test (call-count + no generic sound on player death).
- [ ] **AC4 — Extra juice layers (assumption-marked):** At least two additional
  layered effects beyond particles + shake + sound, each configurable and
  testable. Proposed set `[ASSUMPTION]`: (a) a brief full-screen white/cyan
  **flash** (alpha fades ~1 → 0 over ~120–200 ms) and (b) **debris shards** or
  an expanding **shockwave ring** that outlive the particle burst briefly. Each
  layer is individually toggleable via a constant so the producer can drop any
  they dislike without code surgery.
- [ ] **AC5 — Severity scaling & no behaviour change:** The effect is heavier
  for run-ending death (final life / game over) than for a mid-run respawn
  `[ASSUMPTION]`, via a `severity` parameter. Respawn position, invulnerability
  duration, blink, lives/score accounting, and shield-absorption behaviour are
  unchanged; no changes to hit detection.
- [ ] **AC6 — Teardown / no leaks:** All juice-owned GameObjects (flash
  overlay, debris, shockwave, particles) are tracked and destroyed on scene
  `SHUTDOWN`; stop→restart of a scene instance leaks nothing (mirrors the
  existing `playerExplosions` registry pattern).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: shake fired with
  configured params; dedicated sound called exactly once and generic sound not
  called on the player path; flash fades and is destroyed; debris/shockwave
  lifecycle; severity scaling; teardown leaks nothing. Existing player/scene
  suites still pass (update any assertions that assume the old single-burst
  behaviour).
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** GDD §7.2 (and §7.3 audio if the new cue is
  listed) updated to describe the player-death juice; code comments on new
  constants/helpers; README updated if it documents audio/VFX behaviour.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes**
  (`npm test` = `vitest run`) and `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`).

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser 4.2.1 + TypeScript 7, Vite, Vitest 4 (existing stack).
  Prefer Phaser `camera.shake()` for shake and Graphics/tween layers for the
  rest, consistent with the existing Graphics-particle approach in
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`.
- **Performance:** must not drop FPS on web; layers are short-lived and pooled
  or destroyed promptly; no per-frame allocation leaks.
- **Neon aesthetic:** consistent with GDD §7.1 palette; player effects centre
  on `SHIP_COLOR 0x00ffff`.
- **No behaviour change beyond VFX/audio:** respawn, invulnerability, lives,
  score, and shield logic untouched; no double audio.
- **Testability:** pure logic (intensity/duration/severity mapping) separated
  from Phaser rendering so it is unit-testable with fakes/spies.
- **No heavy new audio assets assumed:** sounds are synthesised with the
  Web Audio `blip`/oscillator helpers already in `src/audio/effects.ts`
  `[ASSUMPTION]` (no binary asset pipeline in this repo).

## Existing state

- **Player-death particle burst already exists** (shipped in
  AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V, v0.1.3): `spawnExplosionParticles(scene, x, y,
  SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE, { patterns: resolvePatterns('player'), registry })`,
  called from `PlayScene._spawnPlayerExplosion()` and
  `GymFormationScene._spawnPlayerExplosion()`.
- **Sound:** both player paths call the generic enemy cue
  `playDestructionSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:430`, a 0.28 s descending
  sawtooth blip at volume 0.3). No player-specific cue exists.
- **Scale pulse:** both paths tween the ship to `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK` (1.5)
  over `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PULSE_DURATION/2` (0.2 s) and back.
- **No camera shake anywhere:** `grep` for `camera.shake` / `this.cameras`
  across `src/` returns nothing.
- **Two death paths:**
  - `PlayScene._hitPlayer() → _loseLife(explodeShip=true)` — costs a life,
    triggers `_finishRun(false)` at 0 lives, else `respawnInPlace()` +
    invulnerability blink.
  - `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` — combat gym: increments
    `playerHitCount`, plays sound + particles + scale pulse, `respawnInPlace()`,
    sets invulnerability/blink.
- Relevant constants live in `src/core/constants.ts`
  (`PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK=1.5`, `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PULSE_DURATION=0.4`,
  `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE=1.5`, `COMBAT_HIT_BLINK_INTERVAL=0.1`).

## Desired change

1. Add a shared player-death juice composition helper (pure severity→params
   mapping + thin Phaser application) in `src/vfx/`.
2. Add tunable constants for shake intensity/duration, flash alpha/duration,
   debris/shockwave counts/lifetimes, and severity multipliers, in one module.
3. Add a dedicated `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (layered, heavier) to
   `src/audio/effects.ts`; replace the generic `playDestructionSound()` call on
   the two player-death paths only (enemy paths unchanged).
4. Trigger scene-camera shake on player destruction, scaled by severity.
5. Add the extra juice layers (flash + debris/shockwave) as individually
   toggleable, teardown-tracked GameObjects.
6. Wire both `PlayScene._loseLife()` and `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` to the
   helper; preserve all existing non-VFX behaviour.
7. Add/extend unit tests and update GDD §7.2/§7.3 + comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` — **new.** Composes shake + flash + debris/
  shockwave (+ delegates to existing particle helper); pure `resolveJuiceParams(severity)`
  mapping and teardown registry.
- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` — **new.** Shake params, flash/debris
  lifecycle, severity scaling, teardown.
- `src/vfx/constants.ts` (or `src/core/constants.ts`) — new tunables:
  `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION`,
  `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, debris/
  shockwave counts, `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (+ constants);
  leave `playDestructionSound()` untouched for enemies.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_loseLife()` / `_hitPlayer()` /
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` call the new helper with severity `'fatal'` vs
  `'respawn'`; SHUTDOWN teardown updates.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` /
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion()` call the helper with `'respawn'` severity;
  SHUTDOWN teardown updates (`playerExplosions` registry pattern).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene*.test.ts`
  — update/extend hit-response assertions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 particle/VFX and §7.3 audio notes.

## Related work

- **Immediate predecessor (completed):** Add particle-based explosion VFX for
  enemy and player deaths (AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V) — delivered the shared
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`, colour jitter, three pattern emitters, and
  wiring to all death paths. Its scope-creep guard explicitly deferred
  **screen-shake, sound redesign, debris physics, and trailing smoke** to
  "linked work items if desired" — this item is that follow-up.
- Respawn player in same spot (AH-0MU3VQ0JR009CSIN) — `respawnInPlace()`
  behaviour that must be preserved.
- Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT) — gym player
  presence.
- One Tank changes colour (AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G) — sibling colour-per-entity
  work; coordinates on palette usage.
- GDD §7.1 colour palette, §7.2 particle effects, §7.3 audio cues.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — "go wild" is unbounded / subjective.** Mitigation: bound the scope
  to a named layer set (shake, dedicated SFX, flash, debris/shockwave), each
  individually toggleable via constants; exact intensities are tunable and
  locked by unit tests, with a manual feel pass.
- **Risk — unanswered operator questions mean the layer set is a guess.**
  Mitigation: all invented scope is marked `[ASSUMPTION]`; the item is flagged
  `needsProducerReview`; each layer can be dropped without rework.
- **Risk — screen shake can cause discomfort / motion sickness.** Mitigation:
  keep duration short (~250–400 ms) and intensity modest; consider respecting
  a future reduced-motion setting (not in scope here — record as linked work
  item if the producer wants it).
- **Risk — test churn on hit-response suites.** Mitigation: update assertions
  to cover the new helper call/seams; keep behaviour guarantees (respawn,
  lives, no double-audio) explicit in tests.
- **Risk — double audio regression.** Mitigation: dedicated AC + test that the
  player path plays the new sound exactly once and not the generic cue.
- **Assumption — sounds are synthesised** via existing Web Audio helpers (no
  new asset pipeline).
- **Assumption — severity scaling** ('fatal' heavier than 'respawn') is wanted;
  easily removed if not.
- **Assumption — both death paths** (real run + combat gym) should get the
  juice; if only the real run is wanted, the gym wiring can be dropped.
- **Scope-creep guard:** reduced-motion accessibility setting, screen-edge
  vignette, controller rumble/haptics, score-popup redesign, and full audio
  redesign are out of scope; file as linked work items if desired.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Particle explosions already exist (completed in AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V). Do
  you want these enhanced (more particles, longer duration, additional effects
  layered on top), or is the particle part considered done?" — Operator replied
  "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption: the
  existing particle burst stays as the base layer; *additional* layered effects
  (flash, debris/shockwave) are added on top.
- Q2: "Screen shake — none exists today. Intensity and duration? Single strong
  shake fading over ~200–300 ms, layered, or horizontal only vs full 2D?" —
  Operator replied "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working
  assumption: single full-2D shake, intensity ~0.008–0.02, duration ~250–400 ms,
  scaled by severity.
- Q3: "SFX — should the player death have its own dedicated sound distinct from
  enemy destruction? Layered sounds or a single improved sound?" — Operator
  replied "continue" without an answer. **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption:
  dedicated layered `playPlayerDestructionSound()`, distinct from the generic
  enemy cue.
- Q4: "\"Lots of juice\" — beyond particles, screen shake, and SFX, what other
  juice do you envision? (e.g. screen flash, debris, slow-mo, UI feedback,
  score popup, camera zoom?)" — Operator replied "continue" without an answer.
  **OPEN QUESTION.** Working assumption: brief full-screen flash + debris
  shards/expanding shockwave ring; nothing else.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTGBOKLC006N8UX** – Diver should rotate to face the player and dive towards them (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G** – One Tank changes colour (completed)
- **AH-0MTHG5BSP006A81R** – Gym index discovers all enemy configs (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+313 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mtvybl2l0085g6g, ac3, ac4, ac5, acceptance (+309 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mtvybl2l0085g6g, ac1, ac4, add, added (+246 more)

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan_complete)

**Decision:** Full planning. Effort is **Small** and risk **Medium**; the bundled
pre-check returned `decision: "plan"`. The plan-approval gate returned
`request_approval: false` (effort not Medium+, risk not High), so no approval pause was
taken — producer validation of the OPEN QUESTIONS below is still requested.

**Vertical-slice phasing:** every item is an end-to-end slice (module + tests + wiring +
docs where relevant); between phases the next item's description is re-checked. Test-first:
the pure parameter model (F1) is the test-first spec that fails before implementation, and
the cross-path verification sweep (F9) closes the loop after wiring.

### Features

| # | Feature | Type | Depends on | Effort | Risk | ID |
|---|---------|------|-----------|--------|------|----|
| F1 | Player-death juice parameter model and constants | task | — | S | Low | AH-0MUDY2GH3003NYY3 |
| F2 | Dedicated player-destruction SFX | task | — | S | Low | AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A |
| F3 | Screen shake and flash layers | task | F1 | M | Medium | AH-0MUDY2K1K005V5L5 |
| F4 | Debris shards and shockwave ring | task | F1 | M | Medium | AH-0MUDY2LRR0040035 |
| F5 | Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point | task | F1, F2, F3, F4 | M | Medium | AH-0MUDY2NE5008MLPJ |
| F6 | Wire shared CombatScene.applyPlayerHit | task | F5 | S | Medium | AH-0MUDY2P1J0032LC6 |
| F7 | Wire PlayScene lose-life path | task | F5 | S | Medium | AH-0MUDY2R4S009F0JI |
| F8 | Wire GymPowerUpsCombat hit path | task | F5 | S | Medium | AH-0MUDY2UC3002Y3YW |
| F9 | Cross-path regression and teardown sweep | task | F6, F7, F8 | M | Medium | AH-0MUDY2W27009VC2M |
| F10 | Documentation: GDD sections and code comments | docs | F5 | XS | Low | AH-0MUDY2YGI0054ZO9 |

### Discovered scope correction

The intake brief lists **two** player-death paths (`PlayScene._loseLife()` and
`GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()`). Reading the code shows **three/four**:

- `CombatScene.applyPlayerHit()` — the shared base used by `GymEnemies` / `GymBoss` /
  `GymMinerals` via the default `onPlayerHit` (covered by F6).
- `PlayScene._loseLife()` — the real run, with `'fatal'` at 0 lives and `'respawn'`
  otherwise (covered by F7).
- `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` — a third, independently duplicated path with its own
  `playerExplosions` registry (covered by F8).

`PlayScene.tryAbsorbPlayerHit()` (shield absorb) and `_loseLife(false)` (wave-timeout
penalty) are **not** player-destruction paths and keep their existing behaviour.

AC6→F3/F4/F6/F7/F8/F9, AC7→F9 (+per-item tests), AC8→F10, AC9→F9.

  individually toggleable so any can be dropped without code surgery. (Intake Q1/Q4.)
- **OPEN QUESTION (to producer):** Is severity scaling ('fatal' heavier than 'respawn')

- **OPEN QUESTION (to producer):** Should the dedicated player-death cue fully replace the

- **OPEN QUESTION (to producer):** Is a reduced-motion / accessibility option expected? Out

Hitting '?' or clicking a 'Help (?)' button next to the 'Index' button should pause the game and bring up a screen that lists all the powerups available in that gym scene. It will have the icon and a description of what it does.

---

*Migrated from ContextHub work item `WL-0MTPLA9BT008HWVL` (misfiled in the ContextHub project; belongs to AI_Hell).*

---

## Intake brief

**Headline:** Add a shared `Help (?)` affordance to the three power-up/weapon gym scenes that pauses the gym and shows a code-drawn icon, name and one-line description for every drop that gym can spawn, with the copy sourced from the shared catalogues.

### Problem statement

The power-up and weapon gym scenes are the project's primary tuning and demonstration surfaces, but a player or developer arriving in a gym has no way to learn what each drop on the field actually does short of reading the GDD. The gyms need an in-context help overlay that pauses the gym and shows, for every drop that gym can spawn, the drop's icon, its name and a one-line description.

### Users and user stories

- **As a developer tuning a gym**, I want to press `?` (or click a `Help (?)` button) and see the icon + effect of every drop this gym can spawn, so I can interpret what I am observing without leaving the gym or opening the GDD.
- **As a player/investigator exploring the dev gym index**, I want the help to show the *same* icon I see on the field and an accurate one-line description, so I can recognise drops at a glance.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the help text to come from the shared catalogues so it can never drift from the implemented behaviour.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat` and `GymWeapons` renders a `Help (?)` text button immediately next to the existing `← INDEX` button, and pressing `?` opens the same help overlay. Opening the help **pauses** the gym's simulation (movement, spawning, firing all stop) and resumes exactly where it paused on close.
2. The help overlay lists exactly the drop types the current gym can spawn, one row per drop, each showing the code-drawn icon that matches the in-game drop, the display name and a one-line description:
   - `GymPowerUpsUtility`: P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet.
   - `GymPowerUpsCombat`: P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport.
   - `GymWeapons`: Cannon (permanent default), Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset.
3. Help descriptions are sourced from the shared gameplay catalogues — a `description` field on `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) and on the weapon catalogue plus a Reset entry (`src/utils/weapons.ts`) — so the help cannot drift from implemented behaviour; every catalogue entry exposes a non-empty `description`.
4. Closing the help via `?`, the overlay's `Close` control, or **ESC** resumes the gym. While the help overlay is open, **ESC closes the help and does not exit to the main menu**; once closed, ESC again returns to the main menu as it does today. The `Close` control is focused by default and operable by keyboard (Tab / arrow keys + Enter / Space).
5. The `Help (?)` button is placed adjacent to the existing `← INDEX` button without overlapping it, and the overlay is an opaque full-screen replacement (consistent with `PauseScene`) that is legible at the game's fixed 16:9 resolution.
6. Automated tests cover the shared helper, the `HelpScene`, and its integration into all three gyms (open pauses; content matches the gym's drop pool; `?`/`Close`/ESC resume; ESC does not reach the menu while open). **The full project test suite passes with the new changes.**
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §4.4 catalogue table and §6.4 gym sections).

### Constraints

- **No external art assets** — icons must reuse the existing code-drawn drawers `drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon` (`src/powerups/icons.ts`), per the GDD §7.1 code-first convention.
- **The new `HelpScene` must not live in `src/scenes/gym/`**: gym scenes are auto-discovered by `import.meta.glob('../scenes/gym/*.ts')`, so a file placed there would appear as a bogus entry in the gym index. It belongs in `src/scenes/` and must be registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
- **Do not change existing navigation semantics**: the `← INDEX` button must still return to `GymIndex`, and ESC must still return to the main menu when help is closed.
- **Paused scenes do not receive keyboard input** (`KeyboardPlugin.isActive()` is false while paused), so the `?`/ESC *close* handling must live in `HelpScene`, not in the paused gym.
- The overlay is a dev/gym affordance; the shipped `PlayScene` is out of scope.

### Existing state

- The three gyms each call `addBackToIndexButton(this)` and `addBackToMenuOnEsc(this)` (`src/utils/gymNavigation.ts`); there is no help button, no `?` handling, and no help/legend screen anywhere in the game.
- `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) holds P3–P9 with `id`, `name`, `type`, optional `duration`/`maxStacks`, but **no description**. `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`) holds `cannon`/`spread`/`dual`/`rapid` with `id`, `name`, pattern data and **no description**; `reset` is a drop type with no catalogue entry.
- Each gym already owns an ordered list of the drops it spawns: `NON_COMBAT_ORDER` (`P5,P8,P9`), `COMBAT_ORDER` (`P3,P4,P6,P7`), `ROUND_ROBIN_ORDER` (`spread,dual,rapid,reset`).
- `PauseScene` (`src/scenes/PauseScene.ts`) is the precedent for a full-screen overlay that pauses gameplay and uses `FocusManager` for keyboard-operable controls; it is registered in `gameConfig.ts`.

### Desired change

1. Add a `description` string to every `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` entry and every `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` entry, plus a description for the `reset` drop (e.g. a small typed map/entry alongside the weapon catalogue), derived from GDD §4.4. Proposed one-line copy:
   - P3 Shield — "Absorbs one hit; a bubble protects the ship for 15 s."
   - P4 Bomb — "Instantly clears every on-screen enemy bullet (no enemy damage)."
   - P5 Speed Boost — "+50% movement speed for 10 s."
   - P6 Phase Shift — "3 s of intangibility — pass through enemies and bullets."
   - P7 Teleport — "Stores a use; press S or ↓ to warp to the nearest safe spot and gain 3 s Phase Shift on arrival."
   - P8 Extra Life — "+1 life immediately (starts at 3, capped at 5)."
   - P9 Magnet — "Permanently pulls nearby drops toward the ship (stacks up to 5)."
   - Cannon — "Permanent default weapon — one bullet straight ahead."
   - Spread — "Adds a 3-bullet fan (−30°/0°/+30°) for 10 s."
   - Dual — "Adds two side-by-side bullets for 10 s."
   - Rapid — "Adds single bullets at a much higher fire rate for 10 s."
   - Reset — "Clears all timed weapons, leaving only the Cannon."

## Problem
During parent/epic implementation, `implement.py finish <child>` pushes the child's feature branch to `refs/heads/dev` on the remote but does NOT fast-forward (or otherwise update) the local `dev` branch. The next `implement.py parent <epic>` call creates the next child's worktree from the stale local `dev`, so the new worktree is missing the just-merged sibling's files.

## Observed
- F2 (AH-0MUBYU600004YU4T) finish pushed commit 91538d0 to origin/dev; local dev stayed at 1920e65.
- The F3 worktree (AH-0MUBYXR280018HST) was created from local dev 1920e65 and could not resolve `../powerups/collectAnimation` (added by F2) until local dev was fast-forwarded to origin/dev and merged into the worktree.

## Impact
Every child after the first can be created from a stale base, causing phantom build errors and risking lost/duplicated work. Workaround applied manually during the parent AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W run.

## Suggested fix
After a successful push in `phase_finish`, fast-forward the local parent branch to the pushed tip when the main checkout's parent branch is clean/unchanged (or at minimum, document the required manual `git fetch && git merge --ff-only origin/dev` step).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `implement.py finish` leaves local `dev` at least as advanced as the tip it pushed (when safe to fast-forward).
- [ ] A regression test covers the local-parent-branch update after a successful push.
- [ ] `implement.py parent` creates each child worktree from the up-to-date base.

# Player-death juice parameter model and constants

## Goal
Provide the pure, testable foundation for the player-death "juice": a single
`resolveJuiceParams(severity)` mapping and all tunable constants in one module
(`src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`), so the rendering layers and scene wiring stay thin.

## User story
As a developer/designer tuning feel, I can change shake intensity, flash alpha,
debris/shockwave counts and severity multipliers in one module, and the exported
parameter model is covered by unit tests so tuning does not silently regress.

## Scope
- New module `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` exporting:
  - `PlayerDeathSeverity = 'respawn' | 'fatal'`.
  - `interface PlayerDeathJuiceParams` (shake intensity/duration, flash
    alpha/duration/colour, debris count/lifespan, shockwave radius/duration,
    per-layer enabled flags, particle count/lifespan/scale overrides).
  - `resolveJuiceParams(severity): PlayerDeathJuiceParams` — pure, total,
    deterministic; unknown severity falls back to `'respawn'` (never throws).
  - Exported tunable constants in one module: `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_COLOR`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_COUNT`, `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_LIFESPAN_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_DURATION_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers, and `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggles.
- Tests `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` written FIRST (test-first spec).

## Constraints
- Parameter logic is pure: **no Phaser import** in the parameter model.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR` (0x00ffff) per GDD §7.1.
- Intake assumptions: shake duration ~250–400 ms, intensity ~0.008–0.02,
  flash duration ~120–200 ms; keep values inside those bounds.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ intake brief (AC2, AC4, AC5).
- Predecessor: AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` constants style).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` exists and was written before the implementation; it fails against the pre-change tree.
- [ ] `resolveJuiceParams('respawn')` and `resolveJuiceParams('fatal')` return complete `PlayerDeathJuiceParams` with every field populated.
- [ ] Every asserted `'fatal'` magnitude is strictly greater than the corresponding `'respawn'` magnitude (shake intensity + duration, flash alpha, debris count, shockwave radius).
- [ ] All tunables are exported constants from the single module; no magic numbers remain in the helper.
- [ ] Unknown/invalid severity returns the `'respawn'` parameter set and never throws.
- [ ] `npm test` passes (including the new suite) and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC5 — severity scaling & no behaviour change: the effect is heavier and every tunable is an exported constant.

# Compose spawnPlayerDeathJuice entry point

## Goal
Provide the single shared entry point `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)`
that composes every juice layer (camera shake, dedicated SFX, particle burst,
flash, debris, shockwave) so no scene has to know the layer set, and returns the
handles/registry so teardown can destroy everything.

## User story
As a developer, I call one function with a position and severity and the full
player-death effect plays; each layer is tunable/toggleable in one module and I
cannot accidentally play two sounds or two particle bursts.

## Scope
- `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(scene, x, y, severity, options?)` in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`:
  - resolves params via `resolveJuiceParams`;
  - plays `playPlayerDestructionSound()` exactly once;
  - calls `applyShake`, `spawnDeathFlash`, `spawnDeathDebris`, `spawnDeathShockwave`;
  - delegates particles to the existing `spawnExplosionParticles(scene, x, y, SHIP_COLOR, SHIP_SIZE, { patterns: resolvePatterns('player'), registry, ...severityOverrides })`;
  - returns a handle `{ params, registry }` (registry is the caller-owned array).
- `options` allows injecting the registry and a seed for deterministic tests.
- Tests in `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` using the scene harness plus spies on the audio module and `spawnExplosionParticles`.

## Constraints
- The generic `playDestructionSound()` must NOT be called by this helper.
- Exactly one particle burst and exactly one dedicated sound per invocation.
- No gameplay state reads/writes; purely cosmetic.
- Keep the existing `_spawnPlayerExplosion` particle call as the particle source
  (the helper delegates) to avoid duplicate spawns when scenes are migrated.

## References
- Depends on the parameter model, dedicated SFX, shake/flash, and debris/shockwave tasks.
- Parent AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single call produces shake + exactly one dedicated sound call + particles + flash + debris + shockwave.
- [ ] `playDestructionSound()` is not called by the helper (spy assertion).
- [ ] Particles are spawned via `spawnExplosionParticles` with the `'player'` patterns and the caller's registry.
- [ ] The returned registry contains every juice-owned display object and is suitable for SHUTDOWN teardown.
- [ ] `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Covers parent AC1 — shared player-death juice helper exists: a reusable helper composes the full effect and both player-death paths use it.

# Problem

When auditing a parent/epic whose children have stored audits, the audit runner's parent-first flow (SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F) can block the parent on child verdicts that were never actually produced.

## Root cause

1. A child's audit freshness fingerprint (`_compute_content_fingerprint`) includes the git HEAD sha. Any new commit on `dev` (even unrelated) invalidates every child's stored audit, so `_child_content_changed` returns True for all children.
2. In the default in-main-slot mode (`child_in_main_slot=True`, SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE), the child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis run are emitted as `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking agent session and are left `partial` ("pending main-session review").
3. When the runner is launched non-interactively (e.g. by a downtime worker / shell subprocess), no session services that work, so every child's `ac_results` stay `partial`. `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even though all of the parent's own ACs are met/adjusted.
4. The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes the parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete`.

## Observed

During AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO (Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a shared core scene base class), the parent's own ACs were all met/adjusted (AC8 met via `--green-run HEAD`) and the full suite was green (75 files / 1545 tests), yet the parent audit returned "No" solely because all eight children were re-screened in-main-slot and left pending. Running with `--no-child-in-main-slot` instead hit intermittent local-proxy stalls (child screens timing out at the 600 s `--child-screen-timeout` → `partial`).

## Impact

- A passing parent audit cannot be recorded for an epic whose children were previously audited, whenever HEAD has advanced, in a non-interactive audit run.
- The parent/children statuses are demoted as a side effect of the "No" restore path.

## Suggested directions (not prescriptive)

- Make the child freshness fingerprint independent of the global HEAD sha, or scope it to the child's own key files/commits, so unrelated HEAD movement does not force a full child re-audit.
- In in-main-slot mode, treat non-serviced child verdicts as "not assessed" (inherit parent pass or mark reusable) rather than blocking the parent, or auto-fall-back to the separate-process path with retry.
- Surface a clear diagnostic distinguishing "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" from a genuine not-ready child.

# Tests: CSV codec (parse, serialise, coerce, validate)

Create the test suite for the CSV codec module (`src/core/csv.ts`) before implementing the codec itself.

**Context:**

The CSV codec module provides an RFC 4180 CSV parser and serializer that reads flat CSV rows into typed `EnemyConfig` / `ShipConfig` objects. This task creates the **tests** that define the expected behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CSV parsing — round-trip.** `parseCsvRows` accepts a CSV string (with header row) and returns an array of `Record<string, string>` objects. Each row produces one object; column names come from the header. Empty rows and comment lines (starting with `#`) are skipped.

2. **Type coercion.** `coerceEnemyConfig` converts raw string values to typed fields: numbers parsed via `Number(...)`, enums validated against `EnemyFormationKind` / `EnemyShotPattern`, colours coerced from `0xRRGGBB` hex strings, booleans coerced from `"true"` / `"false"`.

3. **Validation.** Missing required fields produce a validation error. Invalid enum values fall back to defaults. Malformed numbers fall back to `0`. Invalid hex colours fall back to `0x000000`. The validator returns a typed result with errors array (non-destructive).

4. **CSV serialization.** `serializeEnemyConfigs` converts typed `EnemyConfig` objects back to a CSV string with headers in a defined column order. Colours are formatted as `0xRRGGBB`. The output round-trips through `parseCsvRows` → `coerceEnemyConfig`.

5. **RFC 4180 quoting.** Values containing commas, double-quotes, or newlines are properly quoted (enclosed in `""`, with internal `"` escaped as `""`).

6. **Default fallbacks.** When a row has missing columns, `coerceEnemyConfig` fills in sensible defaults from `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` / `DEFAULT_CONFIG` — never returns `undefined` or `NaN`.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/csv.test.ts` — test suite for the codec (to be created).
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts` — type definitions for `EnemyConfig`, enums, and defaults.
- `src/core/config.ts` — type definitions for `ShipConfig` and defaults.

**Deliverables:**

- `src/core/csv.test.ts` — comprehensive test suite covering all ACs above.
- (The codec implementation in `src/core/csv.ts` will be a separate task.)

**Context:**

The Vite plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`) exposes dev-server middleware endpoints for reading and writing CSV files. It runs only in dev mode.

# Vite CSV plugin: dev middleware (GET/PUT, atomic write, validation)

Implement the Vite dev-server middleware plugin that exposes CSV read/write endpoints.

**Context:**

The plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`) registers GET and PUT handlers during development. It uses the CSV codec for validation and performs atomic writes via temp file + rename.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **GET handler.** Serves CSV files from `src/data/` with correct `Content-Type: text/csv`. Returns 404 for unknown paths.

2. **PUT handler — upsert.** Receives a CSV body, parses and validates it, finds the matching row by key, and overwrites it. Returns 200 with the updated row data.

3. **PUT handler — append (Save As).** When the key does not exist, appends a new row. Returns 201 (created) with the new row data.

4. **Validation errors.** Returns 400 with a JSON error object describing which fields are invalid. The file is not modified.

5. **Duplicate key rejection.** Returns 409 (Conflict) if Save As attempts to add a row with an existing key.

6. **Atomic write.** Uses `fs.writeFileSync` to a temp file (e.g., `.tmp_{filename}`), then `fs.renameSync` to replace the original. If rename fails, the original file is preserved.

7. **Dev-only registration.** The plugin only registers its middleware when Vite is running in dev mode (`server.mode === 'development'`).

8. **Registered in vite.config.ts.** The plugin is imported and added to the `plugins` array in `vite.config.ts`.

# Allow `v*` release tags to deploy to the `github-pages` environment (reproducible policy + docs)

## Problem statement

`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` triggers on `v*` tag pushes, but the repository's `github-pages` environment has a custom deployment branch policy that allows only the `dev` branch. Every release tag is therefore rejected by environment protection, so the Pages deploy fails, the failed check run lands on the release-branch HEAD, and the ship release wrapper's `waitForPRMerge()` always falls back to a manual merge.

## Users

- **Operator (release runner):** runs the ship release and expects it to auto-merge and publish without the manual-merge fallback.
- **Player:** expects each release to be live and playable at `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/`.
- **Future maintainer:** sets up or recovers the repository and needs a reproducible, documented way to configure the Pages environment policy.

### Example user stories

- As a release runner, I want pushing a `v*` release tag to deploy to GitHub Pages without environment-protection rejection, so that the release PR's checks pass and the ship wrapper merges the PR automatically.
- As a future maintainer, I want a documented, idempotent script that configures the `github-pages` environment deployment policy, so I do not have to rediscover the `dev`-only policy failure.
- As a player, I want every release to be published automatically at the project Pages URL.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Tag policy present.** The `github-pages` environment has a deployment policy for tags matching `v*`, in addition to the existing `dev` branch policy. Verify: `gh api repos/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies --jq '.branch_policies[] | "\(.type):\(.name)"'` outputs both `branch:dev` and `tag:v*`.
- **Reproducible, idempotent setup script.** `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` exists, is executable, adds the `v*` tag policy only when missing, and is safe to re-run (second run makes no change and exits 0). It fails loudly with a clear message when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated. Verify: `bash -n` syntax check plus running it twice and inspecting the API result.
- **Deploy succeeds end to end.** Re-running workflow run `35993333739` (tag `v0.1.5`) completes with both the `build` and `deploy` jobs `success`, and `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/` serves the game. Verify: `gh run view 35993333739 --json conclusion,jobs` and an HTTP request to the Pages URL.
- **Tag-only trigger preserved.** `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes; non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy. Verify: workflow YAML inspected and unchanged.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Only a `v*` tag policy may be added; the existing `dev` branch policy must be preserved.
- The workflow's tag-only trigger semantics must not change (superseding Github Hosted Alpha (`AH-0MU9P20Q2003D2V0`) AC5 is out of scope).
- The fix must live in this repository plus the GitHub repository setting; the global ship skill must not be edited (out of repository scope).
- Applying the setting requires a `gh` token with repository admin; if unavailable, the operator applies it manually and the script/documentation records the requirement.

## Existing state

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` triggers on `push` of tags matching `v*`; the `deploy` job targets environment `github-pages`.
- Environment `github-pages` has `custom_branch_policies: true` with exactly one policy: `branch:dev`. No tag policy exists.
- Release flow (`merge-dev-to-main.sh`) tags `vX.Y.Z` on the release merge commit, pushes the tag and the release branch, then opens the PR to `main`. The tag push triggers the deploy, whose rejection leaves a failed check on the release-branch HEAD, blocking `run-release.js`'s `waitForPRMerge()`.
- Evidence: workflow run `35993333739` (`event: push`, `headBranch: v0.1.5`) — `build` succeeded, `deploy` failed with zero steps (environment protection rejection).
- No `scripts/` directory exists and README has no deployment/Pages configuration section.

## Desired change

- Add a `tag:v*` deployment policy to the `github-pages` environment (keeping `branch:dev`).
- Add an idempotent, documented setup script that applies and verifies the policy via `gh api`.
- Document the environment policy requirement and the script in README.
- Verify by re-running the failed workflow run so the release tag deploys successfully.

- **Risk:** `gh run rerun 35993333739` may be disallowed or the run may be too old. Mitigation: fall back to pushing a fresh `v*` tag through the normal release flow.
- **Risk:** Wildcard tag policy (`v*`) may not be accepted by the API. Mitigation: verify with a GET after POST and adjust the pattern if needed.
